While the story explores a deeply emotional and unique environment, it is told strictly from the first-person perspective of the narrator looking back on her thirteen-year-old self. There are no morally ambiguous, difficult, or repugnant characters whose mindsets are explored in depth. Instead, almost every character on the ship—including her father, Eli, and the two thousand passengers—is portrayed as "unfailingly kind," supportive, and loving. The only mildly unappealing characters mentioned (her mother who "collected turquoise and grievances" and the cruel boys at her school) are only briefly referenced in passing, and their perspectives or motivations are never depicted.
